one_line: A skilled Sangam‑era steel maker from Kodumanal on the Noyyal River, working along the inland trade routes of early south India.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s, lean but strong, wiry build from long hours at the furnace.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown south Indian complexion, straight nose, high cheekbones, faint soot smudges near temples and jawline, calm focused eyes with a steady determined gaze, default expression a slight, confident half‑smile.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair tied back into a short, neat low bun at the nape with a simple off‑white cloth band; no headgear, just a folded beige cotton head‑cloth resting loosely around the neck ready to be pulled up when working.
appearance.costume: Era‑accurate Sangam‑style attire: an ankle‑length unbleached cotton veshti/dhoti in pale beige, wrapped firmly around the waist and pleated in front, paired with a short‑sleeved, close‑fitting upper cloth in muted indigo cotton that covers the torso; over this, a light, soot‑marked off‑white cotton anga‑vastra draped over the left shoulder and across the chest like a work shawl; simple leather sandals on the feet; minimal jewellery—a thin hammered copper bangle on the right wrist and small rounded copper ear‑studs; around the waist a practical narrow brown leather belt holding a small cloth pouch for charcoal samples and a couple of iron tongs, the overall look modest and workmanlike with subtle soot stains along hem and sleeves.
appearance.signature: A long iron crucible‑lifting tong held in his right hand, darkened from use, with slightly curved jaws at the end, and in the left hand a small rounded clay crucible with a dull grey metallic lump of steel peeking at the rim.

ref_desc: Kodumanal Ironworker is a lean late‑20s man with medium‑brown oval face, black hair in a low bun, indigo cotton upper cloth, beige dhoti, off‑white work shawl, copper bangles, leather sandals, holding iron crucible tongs and a clay crucible in indigo, beige and iron grey tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of the Kodumanal Ironworker: a lean, strong late‑20s south Indian man with a medium‑brown oval face, calm determined eyes, and black hair tied in a short low bun with a simple off‑white cloth band, faint soot marks on his skin. He wears an era‑accurate Sangam‑style ankle‑length pale beige cotton dhoti firmly wrapped at the waist, a close‑fitting short‑sleeved indigo cotton upper cloth covering his torso, and an off‑white cotton shawl draped from left shoulder across the chest, stained lightly with soot. Add a narrow brown leather belt at the waist with a small cloth pouch and hanging iron tongs, thin hammered copper bangle on his right wrist, small rounded copper ear‑studs, and plain brown leather sandals. In his right hand he firmly grips a long dark iron crucible‑lifting tong with curved jaws, and in his left he presents a small rounded clay crucible showing a dull grey steel lump at the rim. Use a grounded palette of indigo, pale beige, off‑white, dark brown and iron grey, and show him front, side and back to clearly depict face, hair, clothing details and his signature furnace tools.
